coverage.notes: Conventions rest on one student's files and two professors' handouts, ENGR 333 evidence covers only its first weeks plus final-exam tips, parametric-table evidence is handout-side only, and no exemplar has been solved in EES.

scope.rule: ENGR 319, ENGR 328 and ENGR 333. Where the courses differ the rule is keyed by course; do not merge them.
scope.basis: Course folders for ENGR 319, 328, 333: handouts, lab manuals, student EES files.

engr328.rule: No $UnitSystem line in the file. The unit system is set in the EES Options dialog and saved with the file, so the equations listing does not show it; the solution-window printout does. Confirm SI/English, mass/molar, C/K, kPa/bar, kJ/J before trusting any number. Individual handouts override the default: one cycle problem requires English units, the flame-temperature problem requires molar.
engr328.basis: All 22 ENGR 328 EES files lack a $UnitSystem line; student notes on GUI unit preferences; ENGR 328 homework sheets naming English and molar systems for specific problems.

engr333.rule: Declare it on the first code line, e.g. $UnitSystem SI mass K bar kJ, so the basis travels with the code.
engr333.basis: Every ENGR 333 EES file opens with a $UnitSystem directive; ENGR 333 printout shows matching unit settings.

tag_every_input.rule: Every given carries a unit in brackets, e.g. T[1] = 300 [K], m_dot = 15 [g/s]. Constants inside lab-manual formulas get units too, or Check Units fails.
tag_every_input.basis: ENGR 328 A/C lab manual (assign units to formula constants); unit tags throughout student files.

convert_not_factors.rule: Change units with Convert(from, to) and ConvertTemp(from, to, value), not typed factors such as 0.133322 or 1000.
convert_not_factors.basis: ENGR 328 IC lab manual (let EES convert units); A/C lab file progression from typed factors to Convert().

temperature_offsets.rule: Use ConvertTemp, or a K unit system, wherever absolute temperature matters (radiation T^4, exergy T0*DELTAs). Convert(C,K) is a size-of-degree factor for temperature differences and does not add 273.15.
temperature_offsets.basis: ENGR 328 boiling and exergy files using ConvertTemp for radiation and dead-state T; homework checklist asking for the right T units in radiation.

unit_strings.rule: Unit strings are case-insensitive: write torque as [N-m], since [Nm] reads as nanometres.

auto_units.rule: Turn on automatic unit setting in preferences and treat Check Units as part of the answer: EES submissions show the solution window with no unit errors.
auto_units.basis: ENGR 328 homework sheets (solution window with no unit errors); student notes on the auto-set-units preference and unit-error counts.

state_arrays.rule: States are arrays: T[1], P[1], h[1], s[1], not T1. Arrays are needed to plot states on property plots, even for a single state.
state_arrays.basis: ENGR 328 Lecture 06A (states as arrays); ENGR 319 week-5 homework sheet (arrays needed to plot a state).

grid_indices.rule: Nodes are T[m] in 1D and T[m,n] in 2D. EES is case-insensitive, so the last index is MM (and NN), not M, and time is written time, not t. Index origin follows the handout: 0-based for the 1D textbook examples, 1-based for the 2D busbar-type problems.
grid_indices.basis: ENGR 328 Lecture 25 handout (MM for M, time for t); ENGR 328 homework 9 and 10 sheets (index origin).

scalar_names.rule: Scalars use snake_case with subscripts after underscores: m_dot_a, Q_dot_evap, T_infinity, h_air_B. Rates use the _dot_ infix, gauge readings end in _Gauge, per-station values end in the station letter.
scalar_names.basis: Recurring pattern across ENGR 328 lab and homework EES files.

plot_arrays.rule: Values used only for plotting get their own arrays, e.g. T_psych[k], omega_psych[k], P_R134a_plot[k], filled from computed states.
plot_arrays.basis: ENGR 328 A/C and IC lab EES files.

fluid_string.rule: A string variable may hold the fluid, e.g. fluid$ = 'Air' then Enthalpy(fluid$, T=T[1]); an ENGR 328 cycle handout asks for this so the fluid changes in one place.
fluid_string.basis: ENGR 328 homework 2 sheet (change fluid in one place); homework EES files using fluid$ in property calls.

reaction_coefficients.rule: For the IC lab combustion equation use the manual's coefficient letters (n, a, b, c, d, e).

engr328.rule: Line comments with //, section banners in capitals (// GIVENS, // STATE 1, // SECTION C-D). Quoted text prints in the formatted equations; quoted text starting with ! prints highlighted. Braces comment out a block.
engr328.basis: ENGR 328 EES files and their printed PDFs.

engr333.rule: Descriptive text in double quotes, e.g. "Problem 1: h and s at each state", so it appears in the formatted printout; braces for temporary checks marked for removal.
engr333.basis: ENGR 333 EES files; ENGR 333 final-exam handout (temporary check equations in braces).

header.rule: Files open with a short comment block: student, course, assignment and problem, professor, date. Demonstration code uses placeholders, never a real student.
header.basis: Header block at the top of every ENGR 328 and ENGR 333 student file (shape only).

apostrophes.rule: Avoid apostrophes inside comments: EES delimits strings with single quotes, and apostrophes in comments were reported to cause trouble. Write do not, not the contraction.
apostrophes.basis: Student comments in two ENGR 328 EES files; single-quote strings in homework files. Student-reported, not confirmed in a handout.

rule: Unit-system declaration (ENGR 333) or a comment stating the GUI unit system (ENGR 328)
GIVENS: raw measured or stated data with units, grouped by physical source; gauge-to-absolute and unit conversions right after the raw value
Constants looked up once: MolarMass, T_sat, textbook formation enthalpies
State properties: one block per state, or one DUPLICATE loop over a run or state index
Balances and derived results, section by section in the order the lab or problem walks through them
Plot arrays and a comment saying what to plot
block_order.basis: Recurring order in ENGR 328 lab and homework files; Lecture 25 handout outline (variables, grid, BCs, interior, positions).

build_order.rule: Build a lab model in passes, solving after each: givens and unit conversions, then state properties, then one control volume or section at a time (simplest section first), then efficiencies, COP or errors, then plot arrays. Clear unit errors before adding the next section.
build_order.basis: Early vs late versions of the same ENGR 328 A/C lab file plus dated intermediate printouts; ENGR 333 final-exam handout (solve after every equation).

two_properties.rule: Fix each state with two independent properties from the process relation (s[2] = s[1], v[2] = v[1]/r, P[3] = P[2]) and let EES return the rest; do not write ideal-gas or constant-cp formulas when the problem wants exact properties.
two_properties.basis: ENGR 328 Lecture 06A; ENGR 328 homework 2 and 3 sheets.

look_up_constants.rule: If cp, cv, R or molar mass is needed, get it from EES (Cp, Cv, MolarMass) rather than typing a table number.
look_up_constants.basis: ENGR 328 Lecture 06A; ENGR 328 IC lab manual.

saturation.rule: Saturated states use x=0 or x=1. Tap or subcooled water is not x=0, which means saturated liquid at Tsat. Above the critical point there is no quality.
saturation.basis: ENGR 328 A/C lab manual (x=0 is not tap water); ENGR 328 homework 11 sheet (critical point).

no_isolation.rule: Equations need not be solved for one variable; write the balance in its physical long form and let EES solve the simultaneous set.

ideal_vs_real.rule: A chemical-formula name (CO2, H2O, N2, O2, CH4, C8H18) is an ideal gas; a word name (CarbonDioxide, Water, Nitrogen, Methane, n-Octane) is a real fluid with all phases. Use Water, not H2O, for steam-table work.
ideal_vs_real.basis: ENGR 328 homework 7 sheet; ENGR 328 IC lab manual; ENGR 319 week-5 homework sheet.

formation_enthalpy.rule: Enthalpy() of an ideal-gas species already includes formation enthalpy; a real fluid's does not. For a liquid fuel, take h_f from the textbook and add the real-fluid change h(T,P) - h(298 K,P) from EES.
formation_enthalpy.basis: ENGR 328 homework 7 sheet; ENGR 328 IC lab manual.

air_variants.rule: Air and Air_ha are different data sets. ENGR 328 asks for Air, not Air_ha, and the IC lab builds air from O2 and N2 for combustion enthalpies; ENGR 333 week-one work used Air_ha. Follow the handout and do not mix them in one analysis.
air_variants.basis: ENGR 328 homework 1 sheet; ENGR 328 IC lab manual; ENGR 333 week-one EES file.

moist_air.rule: Psychrometrics use AirH2O with the total pressure passed explicitly; h and v come back per kg of dry air.
moist_air.basis: ENGR 328 A/C lab manual appendix on EES psychrometric functions.

no_mixing_with_tables.rule: ENGR 319 computer problems: use EES property functions or textbook tables, never both. In every course, do not splice table values into an EES property chain except where a handout requires it (liquid-fuel formation enthalpy).
no_mixing_with_tables.basis: ENGR 319 computer problem 2 sheet; ENGR 328 homework 7 and IC lab manual for the liquid-fuel exception.

reference_state.rule: Absolute h and s depend on the property reference state; compare differences, not absolute values, with tables or classmates.
reference_state.basis: ENGR 328 homework 7 sheet (real-fluid vs ideal-gas reference); comparison of EES and other property packages during ENGR 333 week-one work.

when_ees_is_allowed.rule: Each handout says which problems are EES problems. Several ENGR 328 problems forbid EES because tests have no EES; where a quick EES lookup is allowed the student writes 'from EES' and need not print code. Check before writing EES for any problem.

printout.rule: EES problems are submitted as printed code plus solution window, the requested answers marked as Key Variables with descriptive labels and units, plots included, and no unit errors.
printout.basis: ENGR 328 homework sheets (print code, key variables, no unit errors, plots).

methods.title: Set and verify the unit system
methods.when: Before writing or debugging any EES file.
steps: Read the handout for a required unit system (English, molar, K).
ENGR 333: put $UnitSystem on the first line. ENGR 328: tell the student which Options > Unit System settings to choose and state them in a comment.
Tag every given with units and make temperature tags match the system (inputs in [K] need a K system).
Ask the student to run Check Units and report the count of unit errors and the unit settings line on the solution printout.
pitfalls: Code that is right under K solves silently wrong under C for ideal-gas h and s and cycle efficiencies; no error is raised.
A pasted equations listing from ENGR 328 cannot confirm the unit system on its own.
methods.basis: ENGR 333 EES files; ENGR 328 file documenting a C-vs-K unit-setting error; ENGR 328 homework sheets.

methods.title: Fix states and call property functions
methods.when: Any cycle, device or state-table problem.
steps: Index states as arrays T[i], P[i], h[i], s[i].
Choose the substance name deliberately: real fluid (Water, R134a, n-Octane) or ideal gas (CO2, N2, Air).
Give each call two independent properties by keyword: Enthalpy(R134a, T=T[1], P=P[1]); Temperature(fluid$, s=s[3], P=P[4]); Quality(R134a, P=P[4], h=h[4]).
Write process relations (s[2]=s[1]; h[4]=h[3] across a valve) as equations and let EES return the rest.
pitfalls: cp*DELTAT, Pv=RT or typed table values defeat the exact-property purpose of ENGR 328 cycle problems.
H2O instead of Water gives ideal-gas steam with no liquid phase.
Gauge pressures passed to a property call; convert to absolute first.
methods.basis: ENGR 328 Lecture 06A; ENGR 328 homework 2 and 3 sheets; ENGR 319 week-5 homework sheet.

methods.title: Moist-air stations (A/C lab)
methods.when: Air-conditioning lab or any psychrometric problem.
steps: Enter dry-bulb and wet-bulb pairs per station and the barometric pressure converted with Convert(mmHg, kPa).
Call Enthalpy, HumRat, Volume, RelHum or DewPoint with AirH2O, T=dry bulb, B=wet bulb, P=P_atm.
Multiply per-kg-dry-air values by the dry-air mass flow.
Write each section as forcing versus response; percent error = (response - forcing)/forcing*100.
Copy station values into plot arrays for the psychrometric chart.
pitfalls: Passing a refrigerant-loop pressure as P in an AirH2O call gives wrong humidity ratios with no error.
Electrical power in W added to kJ/kg times kg/s terms without Convert(W, kW) is off by 1000.
Constants in the lab-manual flow equation need unit tags or Check Units fails.
methods.basis: ENGR 328 A/C lab manual; A/C lab EES files (winter and summer).

methods.title: R134a vapor-compression loop
methods.when: A/C lab refrigerant side or any vapor-compression cycle.
steps: Convert panel gauge readings to absolute pressures.
State 1 from T and P (superheated), state 2 from measured T and P, state 3 as x=0 at condenser pressure, state 4 with h[4]=h[3] at evaporator pressure.
State 2s from Enthalpy(R134a, P=P[2], s=s[1]).
Convert refrigerant flow from g/s to kg/s with Convert, then compute evaporator heat, compressor work, COP and isentropic efficiency.
pitfalls: Quality at state 4 outside 0 to 1 means a pressure or state definition is wrong.
Isentropic efficiency above 1 points to a bad compressor-exit reading, not a better compressor.
methods.basis: ENGR 328 A/C lab manual (R134a energy rate); A/C lab EES files.

methods.title: DUPLICATE loops and sums
methods.when: Repeated equations over runs, states or grid nodes.
steps: Wrap repeated equations in DUPLICATE i = 1, N ... END; nest DUPLICATE for 2D grids.
Use MM and NN for last indices and a grid multiplier so node count changes in one place.
Write boundary and interior equations as separate loops over their own index ranges.
Total with Sum(Q[m], m=1, MM), or Sum(Q[2..a]) with the end bound precomputed into a variable.
pitfalls: m and M, or t and T, are the same variable to EES.
Overlapping loop ranges define a node twice and missing ranges leave unknowns; equation count must match unknown count.
Very dense grids can exhaust EES memory.
methods.basis: ENGR 328 Lecture 25 handouts; homework 9, 10 and 12 sheets and files; IC lab file.

methods.title: Transient nodes with Integral()
steps: For each free node: T[m] = T_init[m] + Integral(dTdt[m], time).
Write each node balance all-in (neighbor minus node, always added) equal to rho_cp times node volume times dTdt[m].
Use rho_cp = k/alpha when only diffusivity is given.
Drive time from a parametric table with a time column from start to end.
Validate by switching generation off and comparing with a hand-solvable resistance network.
pitfalls: Half volumes and half areas on boundary and corner nodes are the usual source of wrong results.
The all-in convention only works if every conduction term is added; mixing sign conventions breaks the balance.
methods.basis: ENGR 328 Lecture 27 handout; homework 9 and 10 sheets and files; Lecture 25 validation slide.

methods.title: Parametric table sweeps
methods.when: A result plotted against an input, a time history, or a grid-convergence check.
steps: Tell the student to create the table in the GUI (Tables > New Parametric Table) with the swept input and the outputs as columns.
Comment out the fixed equation for the swept input so the table supplies it.
Fill the input column (first value, last value, number of runs, linear) and Solve Table.
Plot from the table and ask for the table printout and plots back.
Check one row against the single-solve answer before trusting the curve.
pitfalls: Leaving the swept variable also set in the equations over-specifies the system.
Tables live in the file, not the equations text; a code listing does not show them.
methods.basis: ENGR 328 homework 2, 9 and 10 sheets; parametric table printout in a homework 10 PDF; student notes on table setup.

methods.title: Combustion with element balances
methods.when: Air-fuel ratios, heat of combustion, adiabatic flame temperature, IC lab energy balance.
steps: Write one balance per element (e.g. 8 = b for carbon) with air mole fractions as variables; never enter the overall reaction as an equation.
Use ideal-gas species names so Enthalpy includes formation; for a liquid fuel add the textbook h_f to the EES real-fluid temperature change.
Match the basis: a molar unit system returns kJ/kmol; in mass mode convert with MolarMass or mass fractions.
For flame temperature leave T_prod unknown, set H_P = H_R, and give T_prod a realistic guess.
pitfalls: Mixing kJ/kmol textbook values with kJ/kg EES values (off by the molar mass).
Using Air directly in combustion enthalpies; build air from O2 and N2.
Enthalpy_formation does not work for real liquids such as Water or n-Octane.
methods.basis: ENGR 328 homework 7 sheet; ENGR 328 IC engine lab manual; homework 7 and IC lab files.

methods.title: Guess values and limits when it will not converge
methods.when: Solver errors, negative roots, properties out of range, or physically absurd results.
steps: Solve after every added equation; the failure is usually in the last one added.
Set a realistic guess in Variable Info (a temperature in the hundreds of K, not 1), then Update Guesses once it solves.
ENGR 328 guidance: add limits when needed, such as temperatures at or above 200 K, or a film-boiling surface temperature just above Tsat.
ENGR 333 guidance: prefer good guesses to limits and leave limits at -Inf and Inf.
For an inconsistency-in-block error, look for redundant equations: copy the file, comment everything out, and re-add equations one at a time.
Replace singular inputs such as emissivity = 1 with 0.999999999.
pitfalls: A guess near absolute zero sends property calls out of range and returns a mathematical but unphysical answer.
Any thermo result below 200 K is suspect; EES properties are poorly defined there.
methods.basis: ENGR 328 homework 7 and 11 sheets (limits, guesses); homework 12 sheet (emissivity); ENGR 333 final-exam handout (guesses over limits, block inconsistency).

methods.title: A result off by about 1000
methods.when: A property, heat rate or power is three orders of magnitude from expectation.
steps: List the unit system's energy and pressure units, then compare every input tag with them.
Check prefix pairs: Pa vs kPa (orifice pressure drops are often read in Pa), J vs kJ (W-based heat-transfer correlations against kJ/kg properties), g vs kg (flow meters), W vs kW (electrical power).
Fix with Convert() at the input, not a trailing factor.
Remove invented unit tags that are not real units and redundant conversions such as Convert(kW, kJ/s); both leave unit errors that spread downstream.
Re-run Check Units until it reports none.
pitfalls: Hand-typed factors hide the mismatch from Check Units.
A factor near 18, 29 or 44 instead of 1000 is a mass versus molar basis error, not a prefix error.
methods.basis: IC lab EES file fixes (Pa vs kPa, invented unit tag, redundant conversion); boiling and A/C files (J vs kJ, g vs kg, W vs kW); ENGR 328 homework 2 sheet (track kJ vs J).

exemplars.shows: ENGR 328 cycle: fluid$ string, state arrays, two-property lookups, no ideal-gas formulas.
ENGR 333 idiom: $UnitSystem line, quoted comments, state arrays, DUPLICATE over states, Convert(kJ/s,W).
AirH2O stations at P_atm, forcing and response percent error, plot arrays.
Gauge to absolute, R134a states 1 to 4 and 2s, g/s conversion, COP.
MM naming, Integral(dTdt[m], time), all-in balances, validation case, table setup.
Element balances, ideal-gas versus real-fluid enthalpy, back-solved flame temperature.
